Definition: Integration of voter registration data for identity verification, demographic analysis, and service delivery targeting
Comments: No evidence found of electoral register integration with the data exchange platform. Senegal's electoral system is managed separately. The interoperability platform documentation does not mention electoral register linkage among its priority integrations.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0 (Unknown) understated the available evidence. Senegal's electoral file (fichier électoral) is managed by the Interior Ministry's Direction de l'Automatisation des Fichiers (DAF) and Direction Générale des Élections, historically linked only to the biometric national ID card, not to any government data-exchange platform. A March 2026 ministerial progress report marking the New Deal Technologique's first anniversary enumerates the systems connected to the e-Jokko interoperability platform (Treasury e-payments, government correspondence, e-Sénégal single window, e-Consulat, e-Visa) and does not list the electoral register. Multiple searches found no source confirming any data-exchange link between the electoral roll and the interoperability platform. Revised from 0 (Unknown) to 1 (Not integrated), since there is now positive evidence about what is and is not connected rather than a genuine absence of information.
revised_comments: Senegal's electoral register is managed by the Direction Générale des Élections and the Interior Ministry's Direction de l'Automatisation des Fichiers, historically linked only to the biometric national identity card rather than to any government data-exchange platform. The national interoperability platform (e-Jokko), launched in pilot in April 2025 under the New Deal Technologique, connects systems such as Treasury e-payments, government correspondence, the e-Sénégal single window, e-Consulat and e-Visa; official reporting on the platform's first year of operation does not list the electoral register among the connected systems.

Definition: Is artificial intelligence integrated into the data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics
Comments: No documented AI integration in the data exchange platform as yet. The New Deal Technologique (2025-2034) explicitly mentions adoption of AI and plans an AI hub focused on health and agriculture, and the Gates Foundation partnership (September 2025) includes an AI hub component. AI is planned but not yet functional within the interoperability platform.
redteam_note: No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: The original score of 0 (Unknown) undersold the evidence, which the Comments already summarised as showing AI is planned but not yet functional — a description matching scale value 2 (Planned), not 0 (Unknown). Confirmed by a July 2026 workshop (Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy, with Smart Africa and GIZ) explicitly scoping AI use cases — including fraud and anomaly detection in government databases — for a forthcoming national data-value Blueprint tied to the New Deal Technologique, alongside the September 2025 Gates Foundation-funded AI hub commitment. No evidence found of AI functioning operationally within the e-Jokko interoperability platform itself. Revised from 0 (Unknown) to 2 (Planned).
revised_comments: Artificial intelligence is not yet functional within Senegal's data exchange platform (e-Jokko), but its use is actively being planned. The New Deal Technologique strategy (2025-2034) commits to an AI hub focused on health and agriculture, backed by a $10 million Gates Foundation partnership announced in September 2025. In July 2026, the Ministry of Telecommunications and Digital Economy, with Smart Africa and German development cooperation (GIZ), convened public administrations, the private sector, universities and technical partners to define priority AI and data use cases — including fraud and anomaly detection in government databases — for a forthcoming national data-value Blueprint that will guide AI deployment across sectors including health, agriculture, transport, education, taxation and security.

Definition: Level of public transparency regarding data exchange operations, governance, and data sharing agreements
Comments: The interoperability platform includes transparency as a stated goal ('améliorer la transparence dans la gestion publique'). COCOOR coordination committee meets and publishes updates. Annual reports exist from some ministries. No public dashboard for data exchange operations documented. Limited/moderate transparency level.
redteam_note: Value Name differs from the scale label — usually cosmetic.
revision_notes: The original score of 2 (Low - Limited Disclosure) is superseded by evidence of formal periodic reporting. The platform's official website (pins.sn / e-Jokko) publishes a 'Rapport Annuel 2024 - Interopérabilité Nationale' (posted December 2025) detailing achievements, key figures and the 2025 outlook, plus a quarterly update ('Jubbantikoom Numérique', February 2026) citing specific metrics (2.3M transactions processed, +45% growth, expansion to 5 new regions). The COCOOR coordination committee also meets and reports periodically (confirmed September 2025), consistent with the original Comments. This satisfies scale level 3 (Moderate = Annual Reports). The site's homepage also displays placeholders for a live dashboard (administrations connected, active APIs, monthly transactions); if populated in practice this would meet level 4 (Public Dashboard), but the fetched page did not render live figures, so level 4 is not confirmed here and level 3 is used as the safely evidenced score. Revised from 2 to 3.
revised_comments: Senegal's national interoperability platform (e-Jokko) publishes periodic public reporting on its operations. Its official website hosts a 'Rapport Annuel 2024 - Interopérabilité Nationale' (published December 2025) covering achievements, key figures and the 2025 outlook, alongside quarterly updates citing specific performance metrics such as transaction volumes and regional expansion. The COCOOR inter-ministerial coordination committee meets periodically and reports on implementation progress. There is no confirmed evidence yet of a fully live public dashboard, so disclosure currently takes the form of periodic published reports rather than continuous public monitoring.
